title: "Data readiness" is a Myth: Reliable AI with an Agentic Semantic Layer — Anushrut Gupta, PromptQL
talk_summary: PromptQL argues that perfect data readiness is unrealistic and proposes an agentic semantic layer where an LLM generates a deterministic DSL plan, executes it outside the LLM, and learns from user corrections into a versioned semantic layer. The transferable ideas are structured plans, deterministic execution, editable intermediate steps, and correction-driven versioned memory; the 100% accuracy claims are marketing and should be ignored.

takeaways.what_they_do: The LLM generates a domain-specific plan, but a deterministic runtime executes it against data sources and returns results directly instead of letting the LLM generate the final answer.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Let the LLM generate the plan and we will execute this plan in a deterministic runtime

takeaways.what_they_do: User corrections and metadata suggestions improve a semantic layer, and every semantic-layer instance is versioned so teams can roll back to a previous build.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every single instance of your semantic layer is version controlled so a new build is created you can always fall back
takeaways.numbers: Day 30 claim: 47 business terms, relationships across six systems, 12 calculation variants; claims 100% accuracy

takeaways.technique: Sample data to infer schema and meaning
takeaways.what_they_do: When table names are meaningless, the agent samples rows to identify what each table contains and then asks for a correction such as units being cents instead of dollars.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Can you sample a few rows from each table and figure out what table contains the employees

takeaways.what_they_do: The system exposes the agent’s step-by-step plan with an edit control, so a human can remove or replace steps before execution and the agent learns from that nudge.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I can edit their brain. I can tell them, 'No, this is not what I wanted you to do.'

takeaways.what_they_do: They avoid sending retrieved data back to the LLM for answer generation; the deterministic runtime computes and returns the result, reducing reliance on LLM synthesis.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Don't give it back to the LM. Let's not do rag

takeaways.what_they_do: A prompt-learning layer improves the semantic graph and builds the company’s business language from interactions and corrections.
takeaways.evidence_quote: This is a prompt learning layer which basically improves the semantic graph
